arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: H. Bartow Farr argued the Ninth Circuit erred. He claimed the court misapplied the ADA to professional athletes.
Ms. Underwood argued the case tests ADA coverage. She emphasized the importance of applying the law to sports.
Mr. Reardon discussed the PGA's Q School history. He highlighted the league's long-standing qualification process.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Americans with Disabilities Act. It asks if professional sports leagues must modify rules for disabled athletes.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The PGA Tour wants to keep its no-caddie rule. It argues this rule defines the sport.
Casey Martin wants to use a caddie. He argues the ADA requires this accommodation.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The PGA Tour argues caddies are part of the game. It claims the ADA does not force rule changes.
Casey Martin argues the ADA covers professional athletes. He claims the caddie rule excludes him.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the ADA's reach in professional sports. It determines if leagues must alter core rules for disabled players. The outcome shapes accessibility standards for all competitive athletics.
